articles.title_orig: AWS gives developers a free local stand-in for its cloud, built from scratch by AI agents
articles.title_zh: AWS gives developers a free local stand-in for its cloud, built from scratch by AI agents
articles.content_orig:
November 11, 2026 • 1671 words
In 2004, barely a month into my new job at Amazon, I got the opportunity to pick an intern to join my team. I had an advantage over my colleagues: I had already heard about a brilliant young man working toward his PhD at the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam (where I happened to have received mine as well :-)). I immediately picked Swaminathan Sivasubramanian, whom you all now know as Swami. It was probably one of the best decisions I have made in my 22 years as Amazon’s CTO.
After a disastrous Christmas in 2004, when commercial relational databases could not scale to Amazon’s needs, I asked Swami to do a deep dive into how relational databases were actually used at Amazon. It turned out that 70% of database operations were not relational at all. They were key-value. That insight led to Dynamo , which Swami helped architect. When his internship was over, I hired him full-time right away, even before he had finished his PhD .
Bringing in another opinionated academic led to many fantastic discussions with Amazon’s practical engineers, who had become scale experts by actually building at scale. Eventual vs. strong consistency, CAP vs. Paxos, and more. Over time, Swami became one of the principal architects of AWS’s data strategy. And as we have seen in recent years, he has also been one of the intellectual drivers behind AI innovation at Amazon.
I am honoured that he wanted to write a guest post about the fundamental distributed systems work that sits behind many of AWS’s services, and about how the engineer’s work changes when agents write the code. AWS Emulator, launched today, gives agents the kind of test environment that work relied on. Swami’s story is another great example of invisible engineering .
Today we release AWS Emulator, which gives coding agents a local copy of AWS to test against, and it connects to a project from early in my career. In many ways, this emulator launch reminds me of the effort we put into reliable software engineering to improve the quality of the distributed systems we build. To that end, we wanted to share a story:
About twenty years ago, Werner asked me to work with one of Amazon’s earliest engineers, Al Vermeulen, on a distributed lock service we called “Alf”. Alf was built on Paxos, a protocol based on Leslie Lamport’s work that lets a group of servers agree on one value, and a replication engine in it kept copies of the data consistent across servers. Alf, to date, is the service that powers many of our complex distributed systems like S3, DynamoDB and many more (although it has evolved quite a bit with various changes on top â will save it for another blog!).
Paxos is the gold standard among distributed systems consensus protocols and was well understood in academia. However, building it at the scale Amazon and AWS were growing into was not easy. We had to deal with not just replication across servers and data centers but also tens of thousands of clients asking for locks at the same time, renewing their leases during network partitions all the while with the core requirement: Always be correct! At that time, the best ideas for testing distributed systems were large-scale system testing and chaos-based testing. Both worked, but they were expensive, and they could not reproduce many kinds of conditions on demand. That mattered for Alf, which was meant to be the truth store, giving every client a strongly consistent view of the truth, and which had to keep working through server failures and packet loss as well. Several industry papers had written that Paxos-based locking services were hard to get right, and the difficulty of testing them was part of the reason.
We addressed that by simulating Alf’s environment with as much fidelity as we could manage. We ran the servers inside a JVM and simulated the network and the rest of the infrastructure they depended on, so the whole system lived in one program that we controlled. We could drop packets and inject other faults whenever we chose, and we built tools that poked at the simulation for bugs and scalability problems. Concurrency bugs appear only when events happen in a particular order, and in the simulation we could set up many of those orderings on purpose and inspect how Alf handled each one. We also used formal reasoning, through theoretical techniques such as TLA+, and it found many issues as well. By testing this way we ironed out most of Alf’s concurrency bugs before it ran on real servers. Testing in a real environment then turned up different problems, because the real world exposes things a simulation cannot.
Simulation and formal reasoning both improved the software quality of the distributed systems we applied them to. The simulation worked because a small team could build a copy of one system’s environment by hand, and at the time AWS had only a small handful of services. But today AWS has over 200 services, and an application that calls AWS needs a test environment for each one it uses. Building all of those by hand would take years of engineering, and agents now write code far faster than any team can check it in production. So, we wanted to know whether agents could build and test those environments themselves.
The idea came from Matt Goldberg, a Senior Principal Engineer on the AWS Developer Tools team. His hypothesis was that, given a written description of how a service should behave and the real service to check against, an agent could build a working version of that service on its own. For AWS, the written description is the set of public API models, written in Smithy, AWS’s format for describing a service’s operations and their inputs, outputs, and errors. The real service to check against is the AWS cloud itself, the same system customers use.
The agents work from fidelity tests, which are end-to-end customer scenarios devised from the public API models. A test might check, for example, that in Amazon Simple Queue Service a received message stays hidden from other readers until its visibility timeout runs out. The agents correct each test until it passes against real AWS, so the test records how AWS behaves. The agents then build the emulator until it passes that same test, and a test that still fails points at a gap in the emulator. Matt began with SQS alone, and when he gave Kiro one prompt describing this approach, it returned a passable first version of an SQS emulator in about 15 minutes. Matt Goldbergâs launch post tells how that prototype grew into AWS Emulator. All of AWS Emulator’s code was written and tested by agents, and it is built from more than 400 API models covering more than 200 AWS services. It runs free and offline on your own machine. Teams of agents test it against real AWS and fix the gaps they find. Every change goes through a merge gate, a deep bench of automated checks that every change must pass before it enters the codebase, including several security agents doing adversarial reviews.
A coding agent works in a loop: it writes code, runs it, and reads the result before deciding what to change next. In distributed systems that loop runs inside infrastructure, so the services it calls have to behave like the real ones. When they do, an agent can check its own work as it writes and produce correct code on its first attempt far more often, which improves software quality. AWS Emulator puts that infrastructure inside the loop on your own machine.
When agents write the code and check their own work, the engineer’s job is to give them room to work on their own and to build the specs, tests, and merge gates that decide when that work is correct. It was a lesson I learned the hard way when I used Kiro to rebuild the replication engine that Al and I had built for Alf, which took us about four months the first time. I supervised the agent for four nights before I saw that it had no way to check its results. Once it had a spec and a test environment, the rebuild took about two hours.

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Inside Bessent's Situation Room confrontation with Lutnick over China chip security
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Inside Bessent's Situation Room confrontation with Lutnick over China chip security
articles.content_orig:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over his department’s reluctance to label Nvidia customer Megaspeed a possible national security threat in a Situation Room confrontation last week that illustrates the tension inside the Trump administration over Chinese access to Nvidia’s advanced chips, two people familiar with the matter told CNN.
Trump officials have long harbored concerns that Megaspeed has circumvented US law and funneled advanced chips into China — a prospect that Treasury staffers argued should land it on Commerce’s so-called entity list of China-connected companies that could pose national security risks. But the issue gathered newfound attention and importance in recent days when Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a Megaspeed employee suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Senior Trump officials, including Lutnick, also were briefed months ago about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who the intelligence community suspected of being a Chinese spy, people familiar with the matter said.
But despite those warnings, Commerce has so far refused to put Megaspeed on the entity list, the people said.
Confronted on it by Bessent last Thursday, Lutnick did not immediately commit to taking any specific action, they said.
Axios first reported the Situation Room confrontation.
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based company that was originally incorporated in 2015 as a Chinese video game developer called 7Road International. But in the three years since Alice Huang became director and the company changed its name, it has become one of the largest buyers of Nvidia chips in Asia , purchasing more than $4 billion worth of its semiconductors, by some analyst estimates.
Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing and said it is a “compliant and legal company.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy “groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.”
The entity list represents one of the US’s most significant tools for preventing American firms from selling their products to foreign companies and organizations. But adding Megaspeed to the list could also risk inflaming tensions with China amid Trump’s efforts to manage the US’ trade relationship with the fellow superpower. The Commerce Department hasn’t added any company to the list in more than a year.
Representatives for the Treasury and Commerce departments did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic IPO could draw record retail buyers, Vanda Research says
articles.title_zh: Anthropic IPO could draw record retail buyers, Vanda Research says
articles.content_orig:
Americans are increasingly turning to credit cards as financial pressures mount, new reports show.
Collectively, credit card balances climbed by $22 billion in the third quarter to a record $1.29 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's latest household debt report , released Tuesday. Balances are up 4.2% from a year earlier.
Total household debt, including mortgages , auto loans and student loans , also expanded by $334 billion for the July-to-September period to a record $19.1 trillion.
"Overall debt has been growing," the New York Fed researchers said on a press call Tuesday. "This does reflect financial hardship out there."
The average credit card balance per consumer now stands at $6,678, up 2.4% year over year, a separate quarterly credit industry insights report from TransUnion found. The number of people with credit cards rose 2% to 178 million from 174.8 million.
Consumers often turn to credit cards in part because they are more accessible than other types of loans — even though the average interest rate on a new credit card offer is about 24%, according to data from LendingTree . Credit card APRs vary depending on the type of card, the issuer and the borrower's creditworthiness.
"Credit cards continue to be one of the most expensive ways to borrow," said Charlie Wise, TransUnion's senior vice president of global research and consulting.
Over time, an increasing share of new credit cards has gone to borrowers with lower incomes and credit scores, and "those accounts are now showing higher levels of distress," the New York Fed researchers said in a corresponding blog post .
Credit card issuers loosened their lending standards during the Covid pandemic, and delinquency rates rose in the years that followed, the New York Fed researchers said on the press call.
"Macroeconomic headwinds — namely high inflation and rising borrowing costs — have squeezed consumers, with inflation outpacing wage growth for low-income brackets," according to the New York Fed.
Meanwhile, the cost of living continues to climb, with Americans paying more for essentials such as groceries and gas.
Stubborn inflation has now stretched on for years, putting many households in an affordability squeeze. Costs for goods and services rose more than expected again in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics also reported Tuesday.
"Higher prices and higher rates have pushed more people into debt," said Ted Rossman, principal consumer finance analyst at Money Management International, a nonprofit credit counseling agency.
Balances have continued to swell in the wake of the pandemic, and even though the growth rate is now slowing, "from a household finance standpoint, a lot of damage has been done," Rossman said.
The reports come on the heels of the Democrats' strong midterm results, when many voters expressed their dissatisfaction with the U.S. economy , according to Kyle Moore, chief economist at the nonpartisan think tank The Century Foundation.
"The throughline connecting so many of Tuesday's outcomes was a recognition that the American economy is failing American families," Moore said, referring to Election Day.

articles.title_orig: No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister
articles.title_zh: No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister
articles.content_orig:
Scotland's education secretary has said there is no risk to the public after schools across the country were targeted with a fresh wave of hoax bomb threats, less than a month after a previous alert.
At least 1,000 schools received the hoax email, though police and the government said there was nothing within them to suggest a credible threat.
Government minister Mairi McAllan told parliament the situation was "very much in hand".
Specialist cyber-crime officers are working to identify the source of the messages, which were sent to both primary and secondary schools.
Similar "bogus" emails were sent to 300 schools in Northern Ireland , while schools in Italy also received threats.
Assistant Chief Constable Mark Sutherland told the BBC Scotland News that the police were able to assess the threat as a hoax in around an hour and urged parents not to keep their children away from school.
He said: "First and foremost, I'll be sending my daughter to school tomorrow. I think what is important is that we continue to be vigilant, but we are not alarmed.
"We have carried out a significant amount of checks on all of the information we have gathered so far and there is nothing to suggest there is a credible threat and there is no requirement to keep children away from education settings."
He said officers believed that the email was sent by the same source as emails sent to schools in Northern Ireland and elsewhere in the UK but it was "too early to say" who could be behind it.
"We will be working with partners across the UK and internationally to carry out a joined-up investigation," he added.
The education secretary told MSPs that she had held a meeting with police and local authorities.
"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," Mairi McAllan said.
"I would take this opportunity to repeat Police Scotland's advice that there is nothing to suggest any threats to the public from the content of the emails."
The cabinet secretary added there was a "considerable amount of work" ongoing by Police Scotland and partners across the UK to "understand the motivations and the individuals behind this".
Most local authorities contacted by BBC Scotland said schools were operating as normal but some confirmed pupils had been evacuated.
More than 300 calls were made to police when a similar message was sent to schools around the country on 19 October.
In many areas, pupils were off due to half-term holidays.
On Wednesday the majority of schools in Dumfries and Galloway received the email and some were evacuated as a precaution.
A spokesperson for the local authority said: "Each school community/setting is unique and as such has its own way of supporting and reassuring learners and staff.
"We also know that local police have attended some school settings in a community capacity to assist and reassure."
In Edinburgh Queensferry High School was evacuated and pupils were sent home.
Highland Council confirmed a number of its schools "made the decision to activate their emergency protocols".
Local authorities in Glasgow, Edinburgh, East Lothian, Aberdeenshire and Orkney also confirmed their schools received the message.
In Northern Ireland, the Education Authority (EA) said the "message has similarities with a bogus threat sent last month" which was treated as a hoax by the (PSNI).
The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the email originated from outside the UK .
Italian reports said 280 school head teachers had received threats in recent days. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called a meeting of top ministers and intelligence chiefs over the issue.

articles.title_orig: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse
articles.title_zh: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse
articles.content_orig:
Research has found that Britain is one of the biggest markets for child abuse material (Image: Leon Neal/Press Association)
The Government plans to introduce new legislation to further protect children who are victims of sexual abuse by ensuring that sexual material is blocked on all smart devices across Britain. It comes after calls were made by prominent politicians, campaigners and experts to implement new measures.
A white paper launched on Wednesday (November 11) will argue that device-level protections, similar to those that the Government has committed to for blocking images of nudity, can be adapted to prevent child sexual abuse material being viewed on smartphones, laptops and tablets.
Jess Phillips, former Labour violence against women minister, and Lord Nash, a Tory former education minister, will host a parliamentary briefing alongside survivors of online child sexual abuse.
Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter
The white paper by the International Justice Mission (IJM) and experts in law enforcement, child protection and technology will be published as polling showed 80% of people support technology blocking abuse being installed on their devices, with 5% opposed.
Research by the Internet Watch Foundation found 73% of the child sexual abuse material analysed in 2025 was not self-generated and likely captured on adult devices.
The scale of the trade in child abuse material has become global criminal industry, it said, with Britain one of its biggest markets. In evidence of the alarming scale of growth in offending, the UK’s child abuse image database held fewer than 10,000 images in the late 1990s, compared to 40 million today.
The supply of material is now described as “limitless” at a time when AI-generated images identified by the Internet Watch Foundation increased from 13 in 2024 to 3,440 last year.
With children in the Philippines and other poorer countries being abused live on camera to order, Britain is among the three biggest groups of customers in the world for what Europol calls the leading form of commercial sexual exploitation of children.
One in every 100 children in the Philippines was trafficked to produce child sexual abuse material in 2022, according to the IJM. Campaigners also said the supply of recorded material has increasingly become a national security problem.
Lord Nash said: “We are facing a crisis of online child sexual abuse. Seven per cent of British men admit to some form of online sexual offending against children.
“This material is no longer hidden on the dark web but on the apps that we all use every day. By the time the police are involved, a child has already been abused and the images and videos have gone round the globe.
“The material has to be blocked on the phone itself, before the harm is done. The Government deserves real credit for committing to exactly that on children’s phones.
“I urge it now to extend that commitment to every device sold in Britain, targeted at CSAM (child sexual abuse material), and to lead the world in doing so.”
Ms Phillips MP said: “Every day, children in this country and around the world are being sexually abused for an audience, and the images are traded and watched for years afterwards.
“Nowhere is that clearer than in the Philippines, where one child in every 100 has been trafficked to be abused live on camera to order, and where buyers in Britain are among the biggest customers in the world. This should be a source of national shame, and we must stop it.
“The technology, the evidence and the public support are all there; I want to work with ministers to extend on-device blocking to child sexual abuse material on every device sold in Britain, making children here and over the world safer.”
John Tanagho, executive director of IJM’s Centre to End Online Sexual Exploitation of Children, said: “For too long, society’s response to online child sexual abuse has focused on finding and removing abusive images and videos after children have already been harmed.
“This paper demonstrates that we now have the opportunity to do more by moving upstream and preventing the creation, streaming and viewing of child sexual abuse. That’s why we’re calling for a paradigm shift: devices that do not make or display child sexual abuse material. Society deserves smart devices that simply do not work for taking pictures of or livestreaming child sexual abuse.”
A Government spokesperson said: “We are putting in place the strongest online safety laws in the world. This includes preparing world-first legislation to call on the biggest technology companies to make it impossible for children to take, share or view nude images.
“We will also give the police the powers they need to keep pace with criminal use of emerging technologies in order to keep our children safe.”

articles.title_orig: Hundreds of Schools in Italy Are Evacuated as More Bomb Threats Rattle Europe
articles.title_zh: Hundreds of Schools in Italy Are Evacuated as More Bomb Threats Rattle Europe
articles.content_orig:
Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities.
In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger".
"These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook.
Scotland's education secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police.
It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.
"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said.
Scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated.
"Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said.
Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected.
The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools.
The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project.
Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.
Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption.
Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.
On Wednesday one Milan headteacher, Anna Bertato, told Italian media she had checked the email address of the sender online: "It was already classified as spam by a student at a university in Taiwan."
Another Milan headteacher, Massimo Nunzio Barrella, told Adnkronos news agency that he had immediately realised the email was spam when it arrived in his inbox at 08:59 and he decided not to evacuate his school and reassured parents who phoned in.
"The text seemed almost comical," said Barrella, "it was like a message from Martians: 'We have come to annihilate you.' I even had a bit of a laugh."
Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, and pupils were allowed to return to class. Some parents decided to take their children home for the day, but the majority of schools in Milan did not send their pupils home.
Some 280 school head teachers had already received threats in recent days, according to Italian reports.
In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report".

articles.title_orig: Trump Officials Clashed Over Megaspeed, Firm at Heart of Nvidia Affair
articles.title_zh: Trump Officials Clashed Over Megaspeed, Firm at Heart of Nvidia Affair
articles.content_orig:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over his department’s reluctance to label Nvidia customer Megaspeed a possible national security threat in a Situation Room confrontation last week that illustrates the tension inside the Trump administration over Chinese access to Nvidia’s advanced chips, two people familiar with the matter told CNN.
Trump officials have long harbored concerns that Megaspeed has circumvented US law and funneled advanced chips into China — a prospect that Treasury staffers argued should land it on Commerce’s so-called entity list of China-connected companies that could pose national security risks. But the issue gathered newfound attention and importance in recent days when Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a Megaspeed employee suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Senior Trump officials, including Lutnick, also were briefed months ago about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who the intelligence community suspected of being a Chinese spy, people familiar with the matter said.
But despite those warnings, Commerce has so far refused to put Megaspeed on the entity list, the people said.
Confronted on it by Bessent last Thursday, Lutnick did not immediately commit to taking any specific action, they said.
Axios first reported the Situation Room confrontation.
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based company that was originally incorporated in 2015 as a Chinese video game developer called 7Road International. But in the three years since Alice Huang became director and the company changed its name, it has become one of the largest buyers of Nvidia chips in Asia , purchasing more than $4 billion worth of its semiconductors, by some analyst estimates.
Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing and said it is a “compliant and legal company.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy “groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.”
The entity list represents one of the US’s most significant tools for preventing American firms from selling their products to foreign companies and organizations. But adding Megaspeed to the list could also risk inflaming tensions with China amid Trump’s efforts to manage the US’ trade relationship with the fellow superpower. The Commerce Department hasn’t added any company to the list in more than a year.
Representatives for the Treasury and Commerce departments did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: China select board deals with complicated issues
articles.title_zh: China select board deals with complicated issues
articles.content_orig:
China select board members had several complicated issues on their Nov. 2 agenda, not all ripe for decision. They decided three:
— Board members unanimously approved a new, less comprehensive proposal from Raegan LaRochelle to assist with developing China’s revised Tax Increment Financing (TIF) plan (see the Oct. 22 issue of The Town Line, p. 3 ). LaRochelle will receive $3,200 for about three weeks spent educating the select board and the public and working with them and Town Manager Rebecca Hapgood to identify town projects eligible for TIF funding. Her fee will come from the TIF account. — After discussion of the town’s partly-outdated Telecommunications Ordinance, board members unanimously accepted Harmoni Towers’ bond in the amount of $68,637.75. The bond is intended to cover the cost of removal when the tower the company has approval to build on Parmenter Hill becomes obsolete (see the Oct. 29 issue of The Town Line, p. 2 ). The bond amount did not have the professional engineer’s endorsement that the ordinance requires. Codes Officer Nicholas French said confirming removal cost estimates is “not what professional engineers do.” — By yet another unanimous vote, board members changed China’s HRA (Health Reimbursement Account) from the current administrator to Consumer Health Solutions, saving $470 and, Hapgood hopes, getting as good or better service.
The HRA is related to the town employees’ health insurance plan, topic of a quarter-hour discussion and no decision. The Maine Municipal Employees Health Trust currently offers five plans; China is enrolled in the middle one, in terms of employee costs and benefits. The town would save money by switching to a less generous plan.
Hapgood said with the HRA covering employees’ costs, like deductibles and co-pays, last year was the first year the town didn’t “make employees whole.”
She invited select board members to send her questions to be answered at the Nov. 16 board meeting. With open enrollment starting Nov. 15, she expects a decision on Nov. 16.
Another issue involving money and potential complications is dispatching emergency services. Currently, China uses the Kennebec Sheriff’s Office (KSO), which in turn uses the state system. This system, Select Board Chairman Brent Chesley said he learned at a meeting the previous week, is outdated, and the state won’t spend money to update it.
Therefore, KSO intends to switch to the City of Augusta’s dispatching service, at a higher cost.
Chesley was indignant about several aspects of the planned new system. Each town’s charge is based on a 1987 formula, 75 percent on population and 25 percent on call volume, which he said is contrary to state statute.
The formula also hurts China and Chelsea, two Kennebec County towns that contract for KSO patrols, Chesley said. Every time a KSO deputy calls in to check a license plate, China gets billed for a call.
Chesley was more indignant because he had learned that towns with their own dispatching service don’t pay the county anything. He said he asked at the meeting if there is a county service China doesn’t use, can the town be exempted from paying for it?
A final insult, he said, was when county officials proposed starting the new service – and billing for it – on April 1, instead of waiting for the towns’ new fiscal years to begin July 1.
The dispatch bill will be separate from the annual county tax bill, he said.
Also needing decision soon is whether to renew the contract for disposal of bulky waste and construction debris or to seek a new company. The current contract with Waste Management ends Dec. 31. Hapgood said Transfer Station Manager Thomas Maraggio is seeking prices from several services.
Board members heard of, but did not discuss, one more potential expense increase, for Delta Ambulance. The towns of Fairfield and Benton have notified Delta that they intend to stop using its service in February 2027. Delta officials will have to find some way to continue to pay bills without those two towns.
As the meeting ended, Hapgood reminded those present that all town departments will be closed Wednesday, Nov. 11, for the Veterans’ Day holiday; and Thursday and Friday, Nov. 26 and 27, for the Thanksgiving holiday.
The Nov. 16 select board meeting is scheduled for 6 p.m. in the town office meeting room.

articles.title_zh: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
articles.content_orig:
Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain
            the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in
            Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles
            and JavaScript.
The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada 1 , 2 , 3 . Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ 18 O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive ε Hf ( t ) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta 2 , the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin 4 . Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8–16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740–820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

articles.title_orig: Meta’s Head of Infrastructure, Engineering to Step Down in 2027
articles.title_zh: Meta’s Head of Infrastructure, Engineering to Step Down in 2027
articles.content_orig:
Meta's long-time infrastructure leader will leave the company in the new year, setting the stage for a  recently hired former Amazon Web Services executive to oversee its massive data center technical operations.
Santosh Janardhan, Meta's head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering, revealed his upcoming departure on Wednesday in an internal memo obtained by CNBC. Janardhan, who has worked at Meta since 2009, said "it's time to pass the baton" to former AWS senior vice president David Brown, who joined Meta in July from AWS.
The executive move underscores Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's efforts to expand the company's data center operations under newer leaders at a time of increasing investor scrutiny on capital expenditure spending by the social media giant and its hyperscaler rivals.
Brown will now formally lead Meta's infrastructure efforts and serve as chief technical officer of the Meta Compute initiative, which is spearheaded by the company's president and vice chairman Dina Powell McCormick and technical leader Daniel Gross. Zuckerberg is relying on these new executives to continue developing cutting-edge data centers and related infrastructure needed to support its AI ambitions.
The company said during its recent third-quarter earnings report that it expects full-year capex to fall in the range of $135 billion to $145 billion. Meta also logged negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, which S&P Global Ratings noted as part of its decision in late October to revise Meta's credit rating from AA- stable to AA- negative.
Janardhan said in the memo that he will help support Brown through the first quarter of 2027 as part of "the transition."
"As we make the next set of choices about our priorities, this is the right time for Dave to take the lead in shaping that work," Janardhan said in the memo. "Dave has spent his career building and operating dependable infrastructure for a wide range of demanding workloads. He has the instincts, depth and judgment this moment requires."
Bloomberg News first reported on the executive transition.

articles.title_orig: US postpones ‘million-dollar’ China ship tax until January
articles.title_zh: US postpones ‘million-dollar’ China ship tax until January
articles.content_orig:
The United States has extended the suspension of port fees targeting China-linked shipping for another two months, keeping the measures on hold through January 9, 2027, according to a notice published Tuesday in the Federal Register.
The decision gives Washington and Beijing additional time to negotiate over Chinese policies affecting the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding industries.
The Office of the United States Trade Representative said the extension took effect November 9 and runs through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 9. It follows a one-year suspension that began November 10, 2025, under a trade agreement announced by President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The pause also continues to cover additional duties on Chinese ship-to-shore cranes and other cargo-handling equipment specified in the agency’s earlier action.
China also extended its suspension of reciprocal port fees on U.S.-linked vessels until January 10.
USTR said the circumstances supporting the original suspension remain in place and that further discussions with China are needed.
The U.S. fees could amount to millions of dollars for a single vessel’s visit. A 50,000-net ton ship, for example, would owe $2.5 million in charges.
The measures arose from the U.S. investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 into China’s targeting of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors for dominance. The suspended fee categories include charges affecting Chinese-owned or operated vessels, Chinese-built vessels and foreign-built vehicle carriers.
In comments to USTR, supporters of the pause argued that it would avoid higher shipping costs, prevent commercial disruptions and provide time for negotiations. Some sought permanent suspension of certain fees, warning that their return could disrupt trade and harm U.S. exports.
Opponents argued that the fees are needed to encourage investment in American shipbuilding and related industries, including container manufacturing. Some commenters also urged USTR to treat cargo-equipment tariffs separately from maritime service fees and end the suspension of those tariffs.
USTR said the United States will use the additional negotiating period to pursue its concerns with China while continuing efforts to expand domestic commercial shipbuilding capacity, develop the workforce and cooperate with allies.
Why it matters: The reciprocal pause averts additional shipping costs and potential disruptions affecting not only U.S. and Chinese carriers but also businesses worldwide that rely on Chinese-built vessels. It gives importers, exporters and shipowners temporary relief while trade negotiations continue.

CoreWeave is providing the tailwind for futures today, helping lift neocloud stocks, while a rebound for Nvidia is also supporting the chip space.
But is it enough to dull the lingering doubts around the AI trade?
CoreWeave shares are surging in premarket trading, up over 16% overnight, after the neocloud group posted a 168% spike in third-quarter revenue.

The House of Representatives has effectively voted down an attempt to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The House, by a 211-204 margin, approved a measure that will refer the impeachment resolution to a committee, leaving little time for it to be acted on before Democrats take over in January.

The U.S. equity market has repeatedly changed its underlying mechanics while the asset itself — a share of stock — has remained largely the same.
Trading moved from floors and phone calls to electronic venues. Settlement cycles compressed. Commissions fell to zero. Fractional shares and online brokerages expanded retail participation.
The next major change may already be underway.

articles.title_orig: Windows 11 KB5132061 KB5131087 November 2026 Patch Tuesday direct download links here
articles.title_zh: Windows 11 KB5132061 KB5131087 November 2026 Patch Tuesday direct download links here
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft is investigating reports of Windows 11 KB5132061 installation errors, including 0x800f0993, 0x80070306, and 0x800f0989. In our tests, we observed that the November 2026 Patch Tuesday update reaches 99% before it fails, and you won’t make any progress even if you reattempt the installation.
On November 10, Microsoft rolled out Windows 11 KB5132061 as part of this month’s Patch Tuesday cycle, which means it’s a mandatory security update with close to 700 critical Windows-specific security fixes, plus other improvements like a customizable right-click menu.
KB5132061 bumps Windows 11 26H2 to Build 26300.9974 and 25H2 to Build 26200.9974, and it’s supposed to take a few minutes to finish installing. Usually, a Windows update requires a single reboot, but this one may require two or more reboots because of a pending Windows Secure Boot certificate update.
Two or more reboots aren’t exactly a problem, but there’s a bug that’s preventing the November 2026 update from installing. On my PC, the update installed within a few minutes. But some users aren’t even able to get it to finish installing, and retrying doesn’t help.
“I’m stuck in a loop of installing KB5132061, but it’s repeatedly throwing errors such as 0x800f0993, 0x80070306, and 0x800f0989,” one user told Windows Latest, and there are dozens of similar complaints.
One user told us that the November 2026 update failed on four of their PCs with either 0x800f0989 or 0x80070306. They tried downloading the update manually and resetting Windows Update components, but it still failed.
Another user ran into 0x80070306 on two virtual machines and shared the following error:
“Installation Failure: Windows failed to install the following update with error 0x80070306: 2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) (26300.9974).”
I’ve also seen reports of Windows 11 KB5132061 failing with 0x800f0993 and 0x800f0922. One person said it failed seven times, including once when they tried the offline installer from the Microsoft Update Catalog, before it finally installed on another attempt.
Of course, not everyone is affected. Some users have reported that the update installed without any errors, while others say it eventually went through after they restarted their PC and tried again.
Microsoft’s support document still says the company is “not currently aware of any issues with this update.” However, that doesn’t mean Microsoft isn’t looking at the reports, as I’ve been told the company is fully aware of the complaints and is investigating the root cause, including the possibility that Sandbox is responsible.
Windows Latest understands that Windows 11 KB5132061 installation issues could be tied to Windows Sandbox, so if you turn it off, you should be able to install the cumulative update without any trouble.
For those unaware, Windows Sandbox is one of the lesser-known features of Windows, and it lets you run apps in an isolated environment (virtual machine), with the idea of easily testing untrusted programs or downloads. It’s a great addition, and some might have turned on the feature without even realizing it, and now it’s causing the November 2026 update to fail.
One user who looked at their Windows installation logs noticed an error referring to a file used by Sandbox. On their PC, the update failed while Sandbox was enabled, but installed after they turned it off and restarted.
However, I’ve also seen a report from someone who ran into the error without having the option enabled. But if you use Sandbox and the update keeps failing, it might be worth trying:
If you just can’t get Windows 11 KB5132061 to install, you can also try downloading the update from the Microsoft Update Catalog .
If nothing else works, Windows 11 has a Fix problems using Windows Update option under Settings > System > Recovery . It’ll reinstall your current version of Windows while keeping your apps, files, and settings.
For now, Microsoft is looking into the reports, and we’ll update this article when we learn more.

articles.title_orig: John Kerry: America Must Now Follow China’s Lead on Clean Energy
articles.title_zh: John Kerry: America Must Now Follow China’s Lead on Clean Energy
articles.content_orig:
Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’
Cop31 live – latest updates
China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels , and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.
As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.
Green energy is a vital component of the export engine that has kept China’s sluggish post-pandemic economy on track. The success of its exports stands in contrast to its failure to significantly boost domestic general consumption, a structural weakness that has persistently vexed leaders.
In 2025, clean-tech exports surpassed $220bn, and they should grow again this year; the world’s largest emitter is now the world’s leading supplier of clean energy technology. China accounts for about 85% of solar and 80% of lithium-ion battery supply chain production capacity, and in 2025, nearly 75% of electric cars were manufactured there.
Smart moves now by China would position it as a linchpin in a future electrostate world order, persuade rivals to cooperate, and solidify its influence in the global south.
Meanwhile other countries, including the US under Donald Trump, have fallen badly behind. Kerry said they would lose out economically – as well as putting the climate in further danger – unless they, too, embraced low-carbon power and rapid electrification. “The only country that has hugely accelerated is China. The rest of the world is stumbling along while Mother Nature is sending us more powerful signals every week, every day,” he said.
“[China] realised suddenly they had way too much dependency on oil and gas from other places, and they decided they needed to be independent. Other countries, since the war in Iran, and since the strait of Hormuz has been interrupted, have made a similar decision, and they’re moving independently. There’s been a massive uptick in deployment of renewables. Thank you, Donald Trump.”
For autocratic states without free and fair elections , seeing the economic benefits reaped by China would be the spur to adopt low-carbon growth, he added.
“They’ll see where the market is going, and they will recognise where the cheaper alternatives are. Even they can read a spreadsheet, and understand where costs are exorbitant [in fossil fuels], and where you have a better deal,” Kerry said. “Right now, renewables together with storage, together with some transitional gas, is cheaper and more effective, than just going with fossil fuels.”
He added: “The marketplace has made its decision and globally is moving to electrons, and electrostate status. People are going to electricity and they’re going to try to do that as clean as humanly possible. That’s the choice that I see being implemented in many different places. It is unstoppable.”
China has already said it wants Cop31 to discuss the free flow of green technology against a backdrop of “intensifying” geopolitical conflicts – widely seen as a reference to US and EU tariffs on items such as Chinese electric vehicles and solar products.
Li Shuo from the Asia Society Policy Institute (ASPI) puts it this way : “In a world where climate action was once seen as a constraint on growth but is now increasingly a driver of it, China faces a singular question: will it step into a leadership role not out of obligation, but out of self-interest?”
The summit’s presidency has promised this Cop will be one of “implementation and acceleration” – and when it comes to the green transition, nowhere has implemented or accelerated quite like China. As a result, emissions have been in a “flat or falling” trend since March 2024, analysis for Carbon Brief shows .
Beijing sees the energy transition as “central to economic modernisation and energy security, with significant implications for international influence”, said Kevin Tu from the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies. The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East and their effect on oil and gas supplies have only hardened that stance.
The conflicts have also highlighted the geopolitical implications of a planetary shift to green energy. In the fossil fuel era, the designation of the US dollar as the global trading currency for oil gave Washington “what has been termed the exorbitant privilege of being the global lender of last resort”, said Isabel Hilton, the founder of the specialist environment outlet China Dialogue.
after newsletter promotion
“Without that, the US position in the world looks weaker, and if you add China’s dominance of the supply of clean technologies and the supply chains that produce them, US dominance looks more vulnerable still.”
Meanwhile, President Xi Jinping describes China as a “doer and go-getter working for the cause of global development” and state media frequently showcase Chinese renewable projects in countries ranging from Indonesia to Pakistan and Kenya. The value of the green energy deals in China’s belt and road initiative in the first half of 2026 has already surpassed the total for the whole of 2025, a recent analysis showed .
Those countries could be useful allies if China can get the subject of tariffs into the talks. “China is likely to find support from Brazil, India, South Africa and other developing countries concerned about the costs and market-access effects of climate-related trade measures,” said Tu.
China has generally held back from policy ambition or agenda-setting at forums such as Cop. Its attitude to the plans to set a global target for electrification has been ambivalent, even though it would easily hit it, according to ASPI’s Kate Logan. Partly, China has an aversion to prescriptive outside targets, but it is also trying to navigate the divergent interests of its global south partners.
Yixian Sun, a professor of sustainability governance at the University of Bath, said: “I still think there is a mismatch between Chinese policymakers’ views on the role that China can play in global climate governance and international expectations on the influence that China should exert.”
If the world wants China to play a leadership role, the environment needs to change, and more trust extended, he says. “They have to be ready to accept China’s leadership, and I don’t think this is the case, especially for global north countries”.
Analysts will watch China’s actions around climate finance commitments and support for a “just transition” – a framework designed to secure workers’ rights and livelihoods in the move away from fossil fuels.
They will also be looking for signals Beijing will bid for Cop33 in 2028; officials are said to be trying to decide if hosting would be beneficial.
For now, said Logan, “China would be happy with a Cop that doesn’t necessarily produce anything monumental, but comes out with a relatively cooperative outcome … so no major drama.”

articles.title_orig: US to seek Putin’s ‘blessing’ for Europe to join Ukraine talks
articles.title_zh: US to seek Putin’s ‘blessing’ for Europe to join Ukraine talks
articles.content_orig:
ABU DHABI — U.S. officials will head to Moscow in person Thursday to ask Russian President Vladimir Putin to give his “blessing” to allow European representatives to join future peace talks for Ukraine.
Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law who has been mediating talks in Abu Dhabi, told reporters he and White House envoy Steve Witkoff will head to Moscow to meet the Russian leader.
They aim to secure Putin’s approval for Europe to get a seat at the table and to sign off on what would be the biggest prisoner exchange since the start of the war. Kushner said European participation is critical for discussions over revising the future security architecture of Europe — a longstanding Russian demand, and an initiative that has alarmed some European officials.
“We need to have the Europeans at the table,” Kushner told POLITICO. “We have relayed to President Putin directly several times and to his team that the only way to get this done is to have them by our side and I think they are receptive to it.
“I believe that hopefully tomorrow in Moscow, Steve and I will be successful and President Putin will give the blessing for that to occur. I think that if he agrees to that we will be able to make a lot more progress on the issues that matter.”
The talks in Abu Dhabi are the first between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. since February. Ukraine and its allies in Europe had played down expectations of a breakthrough at the talks, and no progress was announced on critical issues such as ceasefires on energy infrastructure, Black Sea shipping or territory.
But the fact the sides were meeting again after nine months without any discussions was seen in European capitals as an important step.
In one move designed to build confidence between the warring nations, Kushner announced that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to what is likely to be “the biggest” exchange of prisoners since the start of the war. The numbers will be confirmed Thursday, he added. Russian state-controlled news agency Tass confirmed that a “large-scale” prisoner exchange had been agreed.
Kushner said that, overall, the two-day talk were “substantive” and “pretty tough” but “a good first step” to get the two sides talking again after a nine-month break.
He said that when U.S. officials met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Oslo three weeks ago, it was not clear that Moscow and Kyiv would be able to resume negotiations.
“It’s been a long way to get everyone back to the table,” Kushner said. “But I think this was a very good first meeting. It was a tough meeting, but a productive one.” He said all relevant issues were discussed between the two sides and that the question of territory “will be the hardest” to resolve.
The Ukrainian negotiators blamed “very strict directives” from the Kremlin for limiting their room to negotiate in Abu Dhabi, making it impossible to make more progress in the talks.
Kushner and Witkoff will aim to persuade Putin to unlock progress on some issues in their meeting with him Thursday and, according to officials who took part in the talks, to agree the date of the next round of negotiations. They will then travel to meet Zelenskyy and potentially European leaders in Dublin on Friday.
Ukraine wants an agreement on a ceasefire by the New Year, as it fears Russia is preparing another winter of bombardments and targeting energy networks to freeze the country into submission.
One critical question, especially for Europe, is how far the talks about changing the continental security framework underpinned by NATO will be tied to the specific negotiations over peace in Ukraine.
Europeans have long campaigned for Ukraine to get the strongest possible security guarantees to prevent Russia attacking again when this war ends. U.S. officials want to explore the idea of providing a NATO-like collective defense agreement with Ukraine which could even see the alliance itself as a guarantor.
But Russia is insisting on widening the talks to include a review of the whole security architecture for Europe — something the U.S. mediators have agreed.
European officials say the sequencing of these talks will be critical. The European side has signaled its willingness to explore overhauling the continent’s wider security system to allay Russia’s concerns — in parallel with the Ukraine peace process. But they do not want to sign up to any broader reforms until peace has been achieved.
Kushner said the aim was to discuss all the issues and then “find a pathway to settle them all at the same time.”
“I think that having these discussions is very important,” he said. “But the implementation of postwar security will not occur until there’s an agreement on territory and on all other bilateral issues.”
The U.S. desire to have Europe join the negotiations throws the spotlight back on the European Union and others such as the United Kingdom to decide who will represent them in talks. EU leaders will consider this now urgent question in Dublin at an informal summit Friday.
Zelenskyy has said he wants to be consulted over who gets to represent Europe, but has urged his allies to hurry up and ideally pick one person to take the lead in future talks .
Kushner said the current arrangement, which includes NATO, the EU institutions, and representatives from France, Germany, the U.K and Italy, was “a really strong way to organize,” adding, “If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation.”
This article has been updated.

articles.title_orig: 400 Mawozo: Headquarters of Haitian gang destroyed, El Salvador's president says
articles.title_zh: 400 Mawozo: Headquarters of Haitian gang destroyed, El Salvador's president says
articles.content_orig:
El Salvador's president posted a video on X of the strikes on a complex he said is the headquarters of 400 Mawozo
Haiti's Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-AimÃ© has praised "the commitment of the Salvadorean forces in the fight against gangs" after a joint strike on a house allegedly used by the leader of the 400 Mawozo gang.
El Salvador's President, Nayib Bukele, had earlier announced that a joint task force had "destroyed" what he described as "the house of LanmÃ² San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang's headquarters".
A small contingent of Salvadorean troops has been in Haiti since January 2025 as part of a multinational force deployed to suppress gang violence.
Last month, Bukele sent an extra 2,000 soldiers to rescue four Salvadoreans who have been missing since they were ambushed on 18 October.
Bukele's post on X , external was accompanied by video of several helicopters firing on a large complex.
As the helicopters circle above, dozens of people can be seen running out of the property, fleeing the strikes.
Writing in Creole, Bukele said "we kept our promise", adding that the alleged gang members "ran away without even trying to fight".
Local media reported that as many as 20 people were killed in the strike, which they said was carried out in the early hours of Sunday.
They also reported that LanmÃ² San Jou, whose real name is Wilson Joseph, was not at the property at the time of the attack.
Posting on X on Tuesday, Fils-AimÃ© thanked the Salvadorean military's commitment "in the fight against gangs" and said the two nations would keep working together, along with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), to "regain control of the territory and restore state authority".
"THE GANGS WILL GET NO SLEEP!" he added.
While he did not provide any further details about the joint operation or the number of casualties, Fils-AimÃ© posted a still from the video shared by Bukele showing a helicopter firing a projectile at the compound.
The BBC has not been able to verify the video posted by Bukele, nor whether the property is indeed the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo, Haiti's largest criminal gang, which is infamous for carrying out kidnappings for ransom.
Salvadorean troops have become a regular sight in Port-au-Prince
The attack on the alleged gang headquarters seemingly came after a user on X had urged Bukele to attack the complex.
"Where is that house? Give us the exact address, and we'll destroy it," the Salvadorean president replied to the post, which has now been taken down, apparently for violating X's rules.
Bukele has threatened Haitian gangs before.
Following the kidnapping of four Salvadorean air force technicians on 18 October, he addressed "the gang leaders and gang members holding our four compatriots hostage in Haiti" directly.
"We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too," he wrote in Creole, referring to his crackdown on gang violence in his own country.
The four abducted Salvadoreans were working as part of the GSF, made up of troops from several nations.
Bukele's decision to send thousands of additional troops to Haiti since their abduction has raised concerns with critics who say they are not all working within the command structure of the GSF.
It has also raised questions about the operational legitimacy and legality of their actions in the Caribbean nation.
Amnesty International has urged both countries to "ensure all operations conducted by Salvadorean forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law".

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Commerce Department received national security warning on Nvidia CEO affair
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Commerce Department received national security warning on Nvidia CEO affair
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock extended its decline Tuesday, falling roughly 5% after dropping 4% in the prior session. The stock came under pressure amid a broader market sell-off and growing concerns about increased scrutiny of the chipmaker following CEO Jensen Huang's admission to an affair believed to involve a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Scrutiny centers on Alice Huang, whom the US government reportedly identified as a Chinese intelligence asset, and her ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dating back to at least 2023.
The Information reported that their rapport could have helped facilitate the shipment of at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips through Chinese companies, according to two people who know her and corporate records.
On Monday, US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Congress needs more answers about the matter, adding that there are "real ⁠concerns that need to be addressed with respect to the ​Nvidia situation."
President Trump, meanwhile, told reporters that the FBI was looking into Huang's relationship, while still expressing support for the Nvidia CEO.
"We'll look into it," said Trump. "I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape."
The broader semiconductor sector wavered on Tuesday amid a broader market sell-off after a hotter-than-expected October inflation reading, which strengthened expectations for a rate hike next month.
Rrival AMD ( AMD ) stock rose 4% before giving up gains. Broadcom ( AVGO ) shares gained more than 1%, while Intel ( INTC ) stock was little changed.
Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ), which manufactures Nvidia chips, wavered, while semiconductor equipment maker ASML ( ASML ) slipped into red territory.
Storage maker Sandisk ( SNDK ) and memory chipmakers Micron Technology ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) declined.

articles.title_orig: Reform boycotts Senedd after member banned for saying white people being replaced
articles.title_zh: Reform boycotts Senedd after member banned for saying white people being replaced
articles.content_orig:
Reform UK will partially boycott the Senedd to protest the ban of one of their politicians for claiming white people are being "replaced".
The party's Welsh leader, Helen Jenner, said Joe Martin's ban was because of "undue pressure" from governing party Plaid Cymru and was an "infringement on freedom of speech".
Martin had been told he would not be allowed to speak in the Senedd's chamber until he apologised for the remarks, which the parliament's Presiding Officer Huw Irranca-Davies called "unnecessarily provocative and deliberately offensive".
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called the ruling "ridiculous and outrageous".
Reform, which is by far the Senedd's largest opposition party, said its members would withdraw from most of Wednesday's proceedings before returning to vote in the parliament later in the evening.
Jenner confirmed her party's boycott on the steps of the Senedd on Wednesday afternoon.
"It is now clear that the freedom of speech of one of our Senedd members is being curtailed, meaning his constituents are being silenced," she said.
"We stand behind Joe, and we will not attend today's plenary session in protest at his treatment.
"Every Reform MS [Member of the Senedd] will be in their Senedd office working hard for our constituents."
Martin said he would not apologise.
"My voters sent me to the Senedd to speak on their behalf," he said.
"I am being blocked from doing so, and now it's clear that I have fewer rights than the people who elected me. That cannot be the situation in a national parliament."
Asked by BBC Wales if he genuinely believed white people were being "replaced" in the UK, Martin said: "That's obviously a fact."
Posting on X, Farage said it was "ridiculous and outrageous that Reform's duly elected Member of the Senedd, Joe Martin, has been banned from speaking in the Welsh Parliament".
"Why is it only Reform that's targeted like this?" he asked.
Martin was also backed by the leader of right-wing party Restore Britain, Rupert Lowe.
He called for the Senedd to be "shut down" if it was "going to shut down legitimate debate around demographic security and immigration".
Martin's Caerdydd Penarth constituency includes some of Wales' most ethnically diverse communities.
On Tuesday Martin asked for a Welsh government statement on the "demographic replacement of white British people" during business questions, when Senedd members are free to raise issues they choose.
Business Minister Heledd Fychan immediately asked the presiding officer whether the remarks were within the Senedd's standing orders - a set of rules that govern conduct in the chamber.
Standing orders give the presiding officer discretion to decide if contributions to plenary sessions - meetings of the full Senedd - use "discriminatory or offensive language".
Delivering his ruling later, Irranca-Davies said: "Until I receive a clear indication that the member understands the boundaries of acceptable parliamentary conduct and apologises to the Siambr [chamber], we will not be calling him to speak."
Senedd officials confirmed an apology would have to be made in the chamber during a plenary session.
The ruling does not cover committees.
Martin is a member of the Senedd's Equality, Human Rights and Social Justice Committee.
Irranca-Davies pointed out it was not the first time he has rebuked Martin. In September, he said Martin had made offensive remarks about surgeons working in the Welsh NHS gender service .
Plaid Cymru Senedd member Carrie Harper called Reform's boycott a "pathetic tantrum" that was a "disgrace to democracy".
"They'd rather play gimmicks and chase headlines than be serious about Wales' future and doing the job they were elected to do on behalf of the people they represent," she said.
In the 2021 census 93.8% of people in Wales identified as white, down from 95.6% a decade earlier, with the country's overall population growing by 1.4% to 3,107,500.
The proportion identifying as Asian, Asian Welsh or Asian British, the next highest group in the survey, rose from 2.3% to 2.9%.
Mixed or multiple ethnic groups rose from 1% to 1.6%, and those identifying as Black, Black Welsh, Black British, Caribbean or African rose from 0.6% to 0.9%.

articles.title_orig: Asian shops targeted as Eswatini cracks down on illegal foreign businesses
articles.title_zh: Asian shops targeted as Eswatini cracks down on illegal foreign businesses
articles.content_orig:
Businesses owned by Asian nationals are being closed across Eswatini as the government cracks down on foreign-owned enterprises.
The crackdown follows Parliament's approval of the Citizen Economic Empowerment Act, which seeks to increase ownership and participation by emaSwati, as citizens in the kingdom are known.
The legislation follows complaints from local traders that foreign-owned businesses are encroaching on traditional retail markets, increasing competition and threatening livelihoods.
South Africa has witnessed more severe enforcement actions, including raids, arrests and the disruption of foreign-run informal businesses, while Kenya has also stepped up action against foreign traders.
Its implementation has sparked a heated debate in Parliament, with MPs divided over how quickly foreign businesses owners should be required to leave.
Mbabane East MP Welcome Dlamini told Parliament on Tuesday that officials from the trade ministry had already begun enforcing the law by closing Asian-owned shops.
Hhohho Regional MP Tanele Magagula called for immediate action, saying "Businesses owned by foreigners in the rural areas must be seized immediately."
But Dlamini questioned whether local entrepreneurs were ready to take over the businesses, arguing that foreigner should be given time tio train their successors.
"Why can't we give the Asians or foreigners at least three years before 'kicking them' out so that emaSwati can learn to run the businesses?" he asked.
Magagula rejected the suggestion, questioning why struggling local traders should have to wait while struggling economically.
"Why must we wait for three years while emaSwati suffer?" she asked.
Parliament subsequently agreed that foreign business owners should be given at least 12 months to leave.
However, unless the law is formally amended to reflect that timeline, the ministry could continue enforcing its provisions.
The closures follow  inspections launched by the trade ministry in August. Some businesses inspected in areas such as Mbabane were found to be fully compliant.
However, the inspections also raised concerns about working conditions an administrative practices at foreign-owned enterprises, including complaints by employees over days off, annual leave and overtime. At least one case remains under investigation.
Eswatini, a small landlocked kingdom in Southern Africa, faces significant economic hardship, with about 70% of its population living below the poverty line.
The government says the new law is intended to expand economic opportunities for citizens, amid concerns that poverty and hunger could fuel further political unrest.
The crackdown comes mid growing pressure on foreign-owned businesses elsewhere in the region, particularly in neighbouring South Africa, where anti-immigration campaigns have led to raids, arrests,looting and the disruption of foreign-run informal businesses.
On July 30, 2026, the March and March movement intensified its campaign against undocumented immigrants, giving them a deadline to leave. Another protest followed on September 30.
The campaigns have been accompanied by violence and attacks on foreign owned businesses.
Two Ghanaian and two Nigerian nationals reported killed amid the tensions.
Kenya has also stepped up enforcement against foreign traders, bring renewed attention to the treatment of foreign nationals and their businesses across the region.
